key_insight: In pathology AI, stronger expert consensus can improve reproducibility without improving clinical relevance, while disagreement may preserve informative signals.
clinical_relevance: Reference standards for pathology AI should be evaluated for outcome relevance, not agreement alone.
method: Compared expert panel size, composition, and consensus across three pathology cohorts.
Examined links between consensus classifications and disease progression or survival in two cohorts.
Evaluated agreement and disease–morphology associations after a modified Delphi process in granuloma images.
evidence_signal: Across 50 lung cryobiopsy cases, 95 lung adenocarcinomas, and 596 granuloma images, larger panels stabilized judgments without improving outcome associations in the first two cohorts; Delphi agreement increased from 0.351 to 0.539 in the third.
watch_item: Potentially informative morphological features require independent validation before they can refine AI reference standards.
paper_title: Beyond Consensus: Human Ground Truth, Expert Disagreement, and Clinical Relevance in Pathology AI
